transcript:
Meeting: Aurora Pharmaceuticals - Onprem / Airgapped Deployment Discovery
Date/Time: 2025-10-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CTO, Aurora), Elena Cruz (CISO), Marco Silva (Infra Lead), Priya Kapoor (ML Platform)

Summary: quick discovery focused on air-gapped deployment constraints, offline model update process, hardware constraints (GPUs, drivers), and security attestations. Customer is regulated (pharma) and needs clear signed update process and audits.

00:00:00 - Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Samira, AE on the Redwood team, and Liam is our systems engineer.
00:00:10 - Rajiv: Hi, Rajiv here, CTO at Aurora. thanks for taking the time.
00:00:15 - Elena: Elena, CISO. We'll be leading the security questions.
00:00:20 - Liam: hi all, really quick, can you confirm that this is a discovery call focused on on-prem, air-gapped deployments?
00:00:27 - Priya: yes, we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs fully air-gapped private. Our compliance team is pushing for air-gapped for any patient-data model processing.
00:00:40 - Samira: great. high-level, we'll capture requirements, constraints, and next steps.

00:02:05 - Marco: so the key constraints from infra: our data center is totally isolated from the internet for the LLM cluster, no outbound access. we have NVidia a100 and a40 nodes but only certain racks are approved, and kernel/driver versions are pinned by our OS team.
00:02:30 - Liam: okay, so pinned drivers and no outbound means we'll need an offline package update mechanism for model weights, runtime, and security patches. we support air-gapped workflows, we typically do signed artifact bundles and an offline installer that our customer can vouch for.
00:02:50 - Marco: how do you handle the signing? do you require hardware HSM or can we use an internal KMS?
00:03:00 - Liam: we can support both. for stricter setups we integrate with customer HSMs for key signing. typical pattern: Redwood produces artifact, signs with our private key, you verify signature with a public key, and optionally re-sign with your HSM after verification. we can also ship a checksum + sig bundle.
00:03:20 - Elena: we need to see chain of custody and attestations. can you provide detailed audit logs for who imported artifacts, when, and what checksums were validated?
00:03:30 - Samira: yes, audit logs are available in the Private control plane. they include import events, checksum validation, operator IDs. we'll share the audit log schema in the docs.

00:04:45 - Rajiv: another question on model updates: do you allow patching incremental weights or is it full image replacements? patching could save time when bandwidth is limited in our internal transfer process.
00:05:00 - Liam: good question. the runtime supports delta updates for certain model formats; for other cases we do full model image updates. delta updates require a compatible format and careful KV cache handling. we'll validate with your model format.
00:05:25 - Priya: our models are standard transformer checkpoints exported from internal fine-tuning. file sizes are ~20-40GB. transport will be via physically transferred encrypted drives — is that supported?
00:05:40 - Liam: yes, we've done physical drive handoffs before. process is: you receive signed bundle, run a local verifier tool (we provide the verifier binary), then import into the private control plane. we recommend STIG-like checks and verifying driver/hardware compatibility first.

00:07:10 - Marco: about runtime compatibility — do you require specific CUDA drivers or container runtime versions? our environment uses RHEL 8.7 with containerd and certain NVIDIA driver 535.x pinned.
00:07:25 - Liam: the runtime has compatibility matrix. we test on 515, 520, and 535 drivers. there are kernel module requirements for some optimizations; we'll share the compatibility matrix. some advanced kernels need newer drivers for fused attention kernels. if your driver is pinned, we can test on your exact baseline in a bench run.
00:07:50 - Elena: network segmentation — does the private control plane need any outbound connectivity for licensing or heartbeat? we strongly prefer zero outbound.
00:08:05 - Samira: for fully air-gapped mode, there is no outbound requirement. the control plane can be installed local to your network. For the hosted/private managed control plane we usually need an outbound to Redwood — but for on-prem air-gapped we can do an offline control plane installation.
00:08:25 - Rajiv: what about telemetry and metrics? we can't send metrics out; we need local observability and logs.
00:08:35 - Liam: observability can be fully local; we ship the Console as a local UI, or we can provide ELK/Prometheus ingest configs. if you want optional telemetry to Redwood we can make that opt-in with explicit opt-in flags, but for your use-case it would be off.

00:09:50 - Priya: for performance, are there any tradeoffs when running air-gapped vs hosted? like batching, KV cache efficiency, or fallback models?
00:10:05 - Liam: performance is the same at runtime; differences come from version of runtime kernels and availability of optimizations like vendor-specific libraries. we can replicate the same runtime if you install the same drivers and kernel patches. What changes operationally is automated fallbacks — in hosted we can route to other regions if capacity is low; in on-prem you'd need capacity planning and Dedicated pools.

00:11:40 - Marco: how do you handle auto-scaling? we have strict procurement timelines so dynamic scaling is limited.
00:11:55 - Samira: for Private on-prem, autoscaling can be controlled by policies tied to available nodes, but in air-gapped regulated environments customers often use predefined pool sizes and manual scaling. We can provide guidance on burst planning and gating policies.

00:13:20 - Elena: compliance: do you have SOC2/ISO docs, pen test reports, and do you support SSO with our internal SAML provider?
00:13:35 - Samira: yes, we have SOC2 and ISO27001 summaries and can provide redacted reports under NDA. SSO SAML is supported for the Console and operator access. RBAC is configurable per-operator.
00:13:55 - Elena: any support for FIPS or HSM integration?
00:14:05 - Liam: we have HSM integrations for key signing and KMS for secrets. FIPS modules depend on your distro; we can run in FIPS mode with the proper builds. we'll document the steps.

00:15:30 - Rajiv: what's the expected timeline to get a pilot up and running if we approve?
00:15:40 - Samira: typical for a 2-week pilot: week 0 is paperwork and network diagram, week 1 install and baseline bench, week 2 run workload and handover. given approvals, we aim for 2-4 weeks end-to-end for pilot start.
00:15:55 - Priya: approvals will take time but we can target a late-Nov roll out if we move quickly.

00:17:10 - Marco: pricing — for dedicated capacity we have to see committed contracts. for private on-prem is there a license fee or support fee?
00:17:25 - Samira: Private deployments typically have a platform license plus support tier. For pilots we can provide a temporary license. we'll follow up with draft pricing.

00:18:50 - Elena: one operational concern: patching cadence. we can't take frequent reboots. how do you handle runtime security patches without long downtimes?
00:19:05 - Liam: runtime supports rolling patching across nodes and live kernel upgrades only for some changes. for critical patches you may need a maintenance window. we can also provide hotfix builds that avoid reboots for certain vulnerabilities. details depend on your OS and whether you accept container restart vs host restart.

00:21:00 - Rajiv: what about model provenance and explainability? auditors want to know training data provenance for models used on patient data.
00:21:15 - Priya: yes, this is a hard requirement for our compliance team.
00:21:20 - Liam: Redwood's platform can attach metadata to model artifacts: training provenance fields, hashes, version tags. provenance is customer-supplied for closed-source models. for models we ship, we keep a provenance record. we'll provide a sample metadata schema.

00:23:00 - Marco: can you run local benchmarks with our private dataset? we can't send data out of the air-gapped environment.
00:23:10 - Liam: we can run the bench in your environment. typical pattern: we ship a bench harness as an offline package you can run, or our SEs can come onsite to run the bench and collect logs. given you can't send data out, we'd run everything locally and share aggregated stats only.

00:24:45 - Rajiv: any limitations on model size or quantization support? we plan to run 30-40B models quantized to int8.
00:25:00 - Liam: yes, we support int8/4 quantization paths; however some hardware kernels for int4 are vendor-specific. for 30-40B int8 you should be fine on A100s but we'll validate with your exact build.

00:26:40 - Priya: about upgrades — you mentioned signed artifacts. what's the operator flow for applying an update? we want a reproducible, audit-friendly procedure.
00:26:55 - Liam: operator flow: 1) receive signed bundle on encrypted drive, 2) run verifier binary which checks signature and checksum, 3) import into the offline control plane UI/CLI, 4) schedule rollout with canary nodes (we recommend 1-2 canaries), 5) monitor local metrics and revert if needed. All steps are logged with operator id and timestamp.
00:27:25 - Elena: can that verifier run in a locked down environment? our kiosks are limited.
00:27:32 - Liam: yes, the verifier is a static binary with minimal deps and can run in your sealed environment. we also support a containerized verifier image.

00:29:00 - Marco: hardware attestation — can you integrate with our vendor TPM attestation? we need to prove the host hasn't been tampered with before importing artifacts.
00:29:12 - Liam: we have integrations for TPM-based attestation on import, and we can require attestation as a pre-check. we'll add that as an optional step in the import flow.

00:30:40 - Samira: quick note, competitors? anyone you're evaluating?
00:30:45 - Rajiv: we're looking at Hugging Face private hub options and an in-house pipeline. Also touching base with AzureML for private endpoints.
00:30:55 - Samira: understood. we'll highlight differences around signed artifact flow and runtime kernels.

00:31:50 - Priya: what's the rollback story if a model regresses in quality? do you keep model version pins?
00:32:00 - Liam: yes, version pinning and easy rollbacks are core to the platform. We keep immutable model artifacts and you can pin route to older model ids. The canary process helps with early detection.

00:33:40 - Rajiv: will you provide a minimal ops runbook for auditors?
00:33:50 - Samira: yes, we can provide a runbook and audit artifacts. we'll send a sample runbook in the follow-up pack.

00:35:10 - Marco: about licensing, do we need to declare hardware upfront for licensing, or can we adjust after pilot?
00:35:25 - Samira: for pilots it's flexible. production licensing usually ties to committed capacity. we'll propose an initial pilot license that can be converted to production terms.

00:36:45 - Elena: pen tests — do you allow third-party pen tests against the private control plane?
00:36:55 - Liam: yes, under coordination and mutual NDA we allow customer-run pen tests on the on-prem deployment. we also share our internal pen test summaries under NDA.

00:38:10 - Priya: what support SLAs for on-prem?
00:38:20 - Samira: support SLAs are tiered. for enterprise we offer 24/7 support with target response times; for pilots we provide daytime coverage. We'll include proposed SLA tiers in the follow-up.

00:39:45 - Rajiv: will you run an initial bench to validate latency with our tokenization and prompt templates?
00:39:55 - Liam: yes, we'd like a bench run. we'll need a representative prompt set (can be obfuscated) and a few sample tokenization rules. Given locality, we'll run bench locally in your environment or provide the harness.

00:41:10 - Marco: what about container signing? do you sign runtime images or do we need to manage that?
00:41:20 - Liam: we can provide signed container images; customers often re-sign with their internal signing pipeline as well. both options supported.

00:42:35 - Elena: for data retention, can logs be configured to avoid storing any PHI?
00:42:45 - Liam: yes, logs and traces can be scrubbed or retained locally only. we can configure scrubbing rules and retention windows to meet regulatory needs.

00:44:00 - Samira: quick recap before we wrap: action items and next steps. We'll send SOC2/ISO docs and sample runbook, Liam will prepare offline update + signed artifact proposal, Marco will provide hardware/driver baseline, and we'll schedule a deeper technical session next week.
00:44:25 - Rajiv: sounds good. please include pricing for the pilot and an outline of the licensing model.
00:44:35 - Samira: will do. any final questions?
00:44:45 - Priya: nope, thanks.
00:44:50 - Elena: thanks everyone.
00:45:00 - Liam: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs.
00:45:10 - Samira: thanks all. bye.

Notes: transcript has minor auto-transcription errors, some speaker labels simplified. References: shared deck (link: internal/redwood/decks/onprem-airgap.pdf), offline-updates doc (link: internal/redwood/docs/offline-update-workflow.pdf).

End of transcript.
